script: Every city begins its day long before sunrise. Bakers switch on their ovens and trucks deliver fresh bread to corner shops. Street cleaners sweep the empty roads while the first trains leave the station. At the harbour, fishermen unload crates of silver fish onto the dock. In the market, vendors arrange tomatoes, peppers and oranges into bright pyramids. As the sun rises, commuters crowd onto buses and bicycles weave through traffic. Office workers open laptops and meetings begin in glass towers above the streets. In classrooms, teachers write on whiteboards while students raise their hands. Nurses start their shifts in the hospital and doctors walk the quiet wards. At the construction site, cranes lift steel beams and workers in helmets weld and hammer. Delivery riders carry hot meals across bridges as lunchtime arrives. In parks, joggers circle the lake and children play on the swings. Chefs chop vegetables in busy restaurant kitchens and waiters carry plates to crowded tables. Artists paint on canvases in small studios and musicians rehearse in basement rooms. In the afternoon, rain clouds gather and umbrellas open along the pavement. Shoppers browse bookstores and clothing shops while buskers play guitars on the corner. Engineers inspect a bridge and gardeners water flowers outside the town hall. Students walk to the library and open thick books at long wooden tables. As evening comes, buses fill again and traffic lights glow red and green. Families cook dinner in small kitchens and neighbours chat on balconies. Lights come on across the skyline and the river reflects the glowing towers. Theatre doors open and audiences take their seats. Night workers arrive at the airport as the last planes land on the runway. Taxi drivers wait outside the station and street vendors grill food in the cool air. At midnight the city grows quiet. A few windows stay lit, a late train rumbles over the bridge, and the harbour lamps shine on dark water. Far from the city, the countryside follows a slower rhythm. In spring, farmers plough dark soil and plant rows of young seedlings. Blossom covers the apple trees and bees move from flower to flower. Lambs jump in the green meadows while a tractor crosses the far hill. Streams run high with melted snow and children splash in the shallow water. In summer, wheat turns golden and the wind moves across the fields in long waves. Combine harvesters cut the crop and dust rises in the warm light. Cyclists climb quiet country lanes and families picnic under old oak trees. Fishermen sit on a wooden jetty by a still lake at dawn. Vineyards ripen on the sunny slopes and pickers fill baskets with heavy purple grapes. In autumn, leaves turn red and orange and fall across forest paths. Farmers stack hay bales and pumpkins lie in the fields. Smoke rises from village chimneys and market stalls sell apples, honey and fresh cheese. Hikers cross a stone bridge and geese fly south in a long line across the evening sky. In winter, snow covers the roofs and frost sparkles on bare branches. Skiers glide down the mountain and skaters circle a frozen pond. A shepherd leads his flock through the snow while a train crosses a viaduct in the mist. Inside warm cottages, people drink hot tea by a wood fire and read books under soft lamps. Under the stars, the village sleeps. Then the ice melts, streams begin to run, and the farmers return to the fields to start the year again.
